newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 30.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct. 30:

WASHINGTON - The Democratic National Committee released information on contributors and expenses during the first two weeks of October, reversing its earlier decision not to release the data until after the election.
WASHINGTON - If Republican Bob Dole won the presidency, it would cement, and probably enlarge Republican majorities in the Senate and the House of Representatives.
WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton has left much undecided about the direction he will take if he is re-elected to a second term in the White House.

WASHINGTON - The National Transportation Safety Board said a Jan. 6 fatal subway crash occurred because Washington's Metro system relied on a flawed computer system and because agency workers were reluctant to challenge orders.
WASHINGTON - Real-life witches will gather on Thursday night to celebrate what they call Samhain, the most sacred night of the year.
WASHINGTON - America Online Inc. revamped its accounting, management and pricing, and said it would take a $385 million "charge against earnings", essentialy a deduction from its profitability.
